info.title: File Management System API
info.description:
Backend for a complete file management system: JWT auth with email-verification OTPs, file uploads with content extraction (PDF/DOCX/XLSX/CSV/text/images) and Cloudinary storage, per-user dashboards, admin statistics, and admin user management.

All authenticated endpoints expect `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. The token payload carries `{ userId, role }` only.

post.description: Creates an unverified user, hashes the password (bcrypt), then emails a 6-digit verification code (valid 10 minutes). Duplicate emails return 409.

201.description: Account created; verification code sent by email

example.message: Account created. A verification code has been sent to your email.

post.description: Consumes the newest active EMAIL_VERIFY code for the account and flips `isVerified` to true. Codes expire after 10 minutes; resending invalidates previous codes.

Invalidates any previous unconsumed EMAIL_VERIFY codes, issues a fresh one, and emails it. Response is generic on purpose (anti-enumeration): identical whether or not the account exists or is already verified.

202.description: Accepted — generic response regardless of account state

example.message: If that email belongs to an unverified account, a new code has been sent.

post.description: Returns a signed JWT (`{ userId, role }` payload) plus the public user object. Unverified accounts are rejected until they verify their email.

error.message: Please verify your email before logging in

post.description: Issues a PASSWORD_RESET OTP (10-minute validity) if the account exists. Response is generic always (anti-enumeration).

200.description: Generic success regardless of account existence

example.message: If that email exists, a password reset code has been sent.

post.description: Verifies and consumes the newest PASSWORD_RESET code, then replaces the password. For unknown emails the error is identical to a bad code (anti-enumeration).
Authenticated. Verifies the current password before applying the new one.

post.description:
Authenticated multipart upload, field name `files` (up to 10 files; the WHOLE batch must total ≤4MB). Pipeline per file: memoryStorage (never disk) → backend derives the real MIME type from magic bytes (client-declared type is only a hint for undetectable text formats) → allow-list check → content extraction ∥ Cloudinary upload in parallel → File row persisted.

Allowed types: PDF, DOCX, XLS/XLSX, CSV, TXT, JPEG/PNG/WEBP/GIF. Every file is processed independently — one failure never blocks the rest. Extraction failures still persist that row as `extractionStatus: FAILED` while the upload itself succeeds.

Status codes: `201` all uploaded · `207` partial success (mixed results) · `400` nothing persisted due to client errors · `502` nothing persisted due to storage failure.

`type` accepts an exact MIME (`application/pdf`) or a family (`image`, `image/*`). `sortBy` whitelist: createdAt, updatedAt, size, filename, mimeType.
